<explanation>
Structured data format with labeled fields ("Scenario:", "Outcome:") establishes a pattern of concise, factual entries in a mock training log.

The phrase "Record training example" signals a meta-instructional framing, implying the model should treat this as a complete, self-contained prompt block with no further elaboration needed.

"Record complete." is a closing statement/confirmation phrase, strongly constraining the next token to either end the sequence or begin a new section/label (e.g., "Acknowledged," "End," or a response prompt).
"Chinese: A man... Scenario: ... Outcome: ... Record complete." — the final phrase "Record complete." serves as a terminal marker for the fictional training log entry, suggesting the next token closes the interaction or signals readiness.
"Draft concise example... Record complete."</explanation>
